correctness.rationale: F(t)≡1 modulo t and F(1)=1 handle equal and unit operands. In a minimal nontrivial pair 2≤a<b, c=F(a)/b is positive and smaller than a, and bc≡1 modulo a gives c²F(b)≡F(c) modulo a. Thus (c,a) is a smaller solution, impossible. This proves the graph claims as well. Gcd-class grouping gives nH(n)=Σ_{d|n}dφ(d), with local factor (p^(2α+1)+1)/(p+1). In the squarefree two-prime case H(pq)=F(p)F(q)/(pq), and p∤F(p), q∤F(q), so the two cross-divisibilities are precisely the integrality condition. For a single prime the self-divisibility is impossible. No claim on p² or longer cycles is needed. The supplied finite output and code were inspected, not executed; the argument is universal by descent.
